about: The reference agenda and presenter script (docs/07-agenda-and-script-guide.md). Written by hand from the board as it stood on 2026-11-12. Load it with scripts/apply-agenda.mjs; `ask` is computed there, never stored in this file.

agenda.title: Warm-up: the tool you'd refuse to give up
agenda.detail: Word cloud on phones, one tap each before anything serious. It's Desk Tour Month, so the biggest word sets up Show & Tell.

points: Wait for ten-odd answers before you read the cloud. Don't discuss it yet: two minutes, hard stop.
Read the biggest word aloud and park it: "Whoever typed that, you're showing it to us in Show & Tell." Volunteers only.
If one editor owns the cloud, ask who the holdout is. There's always one.
prep.opener: Before anything serious, one word on your phone: the tool you'd refuse to give up. Editor, terminal, a shortcut, a mug. All of it counts.

agenda.title: Radar: who do we trust with our code?
agenda.detail: eMudhra intermediate CA compromise (Cloudflare found keys as small as 4) · GLM-5.3 on Workers AI leaked KV cache between users' requests · Google tests an AI-powered gaming platform (a member's link)

points: eMudhra: an intermediate CA was compromised, and Cloudflare found keys set to numbers as small as 4. The private keys could be recovered straight from the public certificates.
GLM-5.3 on Workers AI: a context-window mismatch in SGLang let KV cache pages leak between separate users' requests. The fix: memory pool limits must match the model's config.
Google is testing an AI-powered gaming platform: a member posted this one, not the digest. Then read the poll and ask the smallest camp to defend it.
prep.opener: Two of these three are someone else's infrastructure failing quietly. Vote before I read them: would you send production code to a hosted AI model?

agenda.title: Show & Tell: Desk Tour
agenda.detail: Spotlight and Demo: invites out, neither confirmed yet. If a slot is empty, run a lightning desk tour: 3 or 4 volunteers, 3 minutes each, share your screen and show the one trick we should steal.

points: Lightning rules if a slot is empty: share your screen, three minutes, one trick. Start with whoever owns the warm-up's biggest word.
From the board: Simon Willison built a feature for his blog almost entirely by voice. Ask: has anyone tried dictating code, and where did it fall apart?
After each tour, one question to the room: "Who's installing that today?" Hands up is the whole feedback loop.
prep.opener: Desk Tour Month. Share your screen and show us one thing on it we should steal. Three minutes, no slides, mess welcome.

agenda.title: AI Bubble Bust: the tech vs the business
agenda.detail: Posted anonymously, so the host frames it (3 min). Poll first, then the debate: a crash in AI stocks is not AI going away. Which side are you on, and what does it change about the tools we pick?

points: The post's split: AI stocks crashing is not AI going away. The tech is useful and still improving; the risk is companies spending huge sums with no clear way to earn it back.
Dot-com is the template the post points at: plenty of companies died, the internet didn't. Ask the "pops" camp which AI vendor they'd bet on surviving, and why.
Land it on our work: if your main AI tool doubled its price or shut down next quarter, what's the plan? One concrete answer beats ten opinions.
prep.opener: Vote before you overthink it: does AI pop by 2028? Then the real question: which tool you use every day disappears first if it does?

agenda.title: Problem clinic: name the blocker
agenda.detail: No problem posts on the board this month, so the room sets the agenda: a word cloud of one-word blockers, then the two biggest words get three minutes each.

points: Take the two biggest words. For each: "Who hit this last week, and what did you try?" The first answer gets the floor for a minute.
Don't solve it live. Aim for one owner and one next step per blocker, and write it as a decision note.
Anything bigger than three minutes goes on next month's board as a problem post. Ask who'll post it before moving on.
prep.opener: One word on your phone: what slowed you down most this month? Builds, reviews, flaky tests, waiting on access. Nobody sees who typed what.

agenda.title: Data structures in unexpected places
agenda.detail: Posted anonymously: the host reads the three examples (Git history as a linked list, MongoDB indexes as B-trees, the Kubernetes scheduler's priority queue), then asks the room for one more. The warm-up for the Boss Round.

points: Unmuting is optional: answers in the call chat count. Read the first two aloud.
If nobody bites: where in our own code did we reach for a plain list or map and later wish we hadn't?
Four minutes, then straight into the Boss Round. The data structures are about to get personal.
prep.opener: Git history is a linked list. Mongo indexes are B-trees. The Kubernetes scheduler is a priority queue. Name one you've caught hiding in a tool we use here.

agenda.title: Kers' Boss Round
agenda.detail: Sum of the even numbers, in JavaScript, in your own browser. It runs until the presenter closes it. The screen shows only the % who pass: no names, no code.

points: The problem: sumEvens(nums). Six tests, including an empty array and negative numbers. Run the tests as often as you like.
Nobody sees your code or your name, only the pass rate. Admins play too, presenter included.
When most of the room has had a go, close the round and Kers gives his verdict. Under half passing? Ask the room what tripped them: the empty array or the negatives.
prep.opener: You lot tell me what to write all day. Let’s see if you can still code.

agenda.title: Wrap
agenda.detail: Decisions and owners from the notes, who shows something in December, and one Radar link from each of you.

points: Read the decision notes back with their owners. A decision with no owner isn't one: assign it or drop it.
December's Show & Tell: ask for one volunteer now. A volunteer beats Kers' draw.
This month's Radar was mostly the digest. One link each before next month changes that.
prep.opener: Before you go: what's one thing from today you'll actually try this week? Chat or mic, one line.
